title: What is Descriptive Writing?
author: 6827033fd074fc53eba337c1
chapter_outcomes: Write effectively, creatively, accurately and appropriately, for a range of audiences and purposes

Demonstrate understanding of the conventions of a wide range of written textual forms: advertisements, brochures, leaflets, editorials, news stories, articles, reviews, blogs, investigative journalism, letters, podcasts, (auto)biographies, travel writing, diaries, essays, scripted speech, narrative writing, and descriptive writing

Demonstrate understanding of the linguistic elements and literary features of texts: parts of speech/word classes, vocabulary, figurative language, phonology, morphology, rhetorical devices, voice, aspect, tense, modality, narrative perspective, word ordering and sentence structure, paragraph- and text-level structure, formality/informality of tone, pragmatics
Demonstrate understanding of the significance of audience in both the design and reception of texts
Demonstrate understanding of the ways in which genre, purpose and context contribute to the meaning of texts

Produce an appropriate structure for longer pieces of writing: Freytag's Pyramid in imaginative writing; dialectical structure in discursive writing; introductory, summary and evaluative sections in review writing
Organise writing to achieve specific effects: withholding key information in imaginative writing; juxtaposing counterarguments in discursive writing; evidentiary logic in critical writing
Structure paragraphs: topic sentences, connectives, internal coherence, discourse markers
Use a range of appropriate linguistic elements and literary features: imagery in descriptive writing; rhetorical devices in argumentative writing; evaluative lexis in critical writing
Express ideas accurately and clearly at both sentence and word level
Produce a continuous piece of writing of 600–900 words
Develop writing in a manner appropriate to the form, purpose and audience
